## 1. Executive Summary

- **Session ID:** `ygm/20260804_221748`
- **Application:** YGM (github.com/llnl/ygm) — header-only C++ MPI async-messaging library — plus its companion benchmark `ygm-bench` (github.com/llnl/ygm-bench)
- **System:** Tuolumne (Cray PE, MI300A, no sudo)
- **Pipeline status:** SUCCESS with open follow-ups (see §11). Annotation, build, smoke test, ygm-bench build, and a >=10-minute 128-rank scaled validated run all completed and produced real, non-empty traces. Two real bugs were found and fixed at the framework/tool level. No optimization-loop "before/after" delta is claimed in this session — this was a build+annotate+diagnose+scale pipeline, not a performance-optimization-and-measure pipeline; the two headline findings (Iallreduce rank-density collapse, hot-loop tracing overhead) are **diagnostic/system findings with a working mitigation**, not code optimizations with a measured speedup number.
- **Top findings (all confirmed, untraced where noted so they are real MPI/system behavior, not tracing artifacts):**
  1. `MPI_Iallreduce` collapses ~400x with per-node rank density on Cray MPICH/Tuolumne (510K hops/sec at 4 ranks/node -> 1,229 hops/sec at 32 ranks/node, `MAX_WAITSOME_IALLREDUCE` ~100% of wall time at 32 ranks/node) — a genuine system/MPI characteristic of this library's termination-detection protocol, not a tuning knob.
  2. Annotating YGM's 9 hot-loop/progress-poll functions (`local_progress`, `process_receive_queue`, etc.) made traced runs 5-10x+ slower than untraced and non-scaling with workload size — root-caused to FUNCTION-mode RAII overhead on a spin-poll path called millions of times.
  3. Default YGM receive-buffer settings OOM at 96 ranks/node (`YGM_COMM_NUM_IRECVS=8` x 1GB = 8GB/rank x 96 = ~768GB/node vs ~502GB available); the correct env var to reduce it is singular `YGM_COMM_IRECV_SIZE_KB`, not the plural name first tried.
- **Top mitigations applied (all confirmed working, not "yet to try"):**
  1. DFTRACER selective aggregation (`DFTRACER_ENABLE_AGGREGATION=1 DFTRACER_AGGREGATION_TYPE=SELECTIVE`, rule `dur < 1000`, 5s flush interval) on the 9 hot-loop functions — kept full annotation AND `dft_cnt`-tagged visibility while shrinking per-rank trace size from >1GB to <1MB.
  2. Settled on 32 ranks/node (128 ranks / 4 nodes) as the rank density that avoids both the OOM and the worst of the Iallreduce collapse, with default buffer settings.
  3. Rebuilt dftracer from source with the GNU MPICH wrapper (matching YGM's own `PrgEnv-gnu` build) instead of the initially-installed prebuilt MPI-less wheel — this is a build-correctness fix, not a performance optimization.
- **Key metric:** final validated scaled run — `around_the_world_ygm -n 5600 -t 1 -p`, 4 nodes x 32 ranks/node (128 total), full annotation + selective aggregation: **660.04s (11.0 min)**, 716,800 total hops, 55MB total traces across 128 rank files, `MAX_WAITSOME_IALLREDUCE`~=646s (98% of wall time — confirms finding #1 is the genuine bottleneck at this scale, not a tracing artifact).

## 5. Bottleneck Diagnosis

No formal `dfdiagnoser`/`session_diagnose_bottlenecks` run exists in this session's artifacts to cite severity scores from. The two bottlenecks found (both manually diagnosed, both confirmed via untraced control runs so they are real, not tracing artifacts) are:

| Bottleneck | Category | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| MPI_Iallreduce collective-wait collapse at high rank density | Communication | Untraced hop-rate sweep: 510K hops/sec (4 ranks/node) -> 1,229 hops/sec (32 ranks/node); `MAX_WAITSOME_IALLREDUCE`=130.2s of 130.1s wall time at 32 ranks/node in the sweep, and ~646s of 660s (98%) in the final 128-rank/11-min run |
| dftracer FUNCTION-mode overhead on a spin-poll hot path | Instrumentation/tracing overhead (not an app bottleneck) | Traced-vs-untraced wall-clock comparison, non-scaling runtime with `-n`; root-caused to 9 functions on the shared progress-poll path being annotated |

Neither bottleneck was addressed with a code-level "optimization" in the traditional I/O/compute/memory sense (see §6/§7) — the Iallreduce collapse is characterized as a genuine Cray-MPICH/library-protocol interaction with no lever this session applied, and the tracing-overhead problem was mitigated via dftracer's own aggregation feature, not an application-code change.

**Mechanism paragraphs for the two highest-impact rows:**

**Row 1 (rank density / Iallreduce collapse):** `around_the_world_ygm`'s termination-detection protocol issues a large number of `MPI_Iallreduce` calls per unit of work. As ranks/node increases, contention for the node's network injection/completion resources and the collective's synchronization overhead scale worse than linearly on Cray MPICH here — going from 4 to 32 ranks/node (8x more ranks) dropped throughput ~400x, i.e. per-rank throughput fell by roughly 3200x. This is consistent with a collective-implementation scaling wall rather than a simple resource-contention slope, and is why `MAX_WAITSOME_IALLREDUCE` consumes essentially all wall time once rank density crosses some threshold. No lever available in this session's scope (env var, buffer size, aggregation) touches this — it is a property of the collective algorithm/library interaction at this rank density on this MPI implementation.

**Row 3 (selective aggregation):** FUNCTION-mode dftracer instruments a function with RAII-style enter/exit macros that record a full trace event (timestamp, duration, args) per call. On a spin-poll progress engine, the annotated functions are called on the order of millions of times per run — even microsecond-scale per-call overhead compounds into the dominant cost. Selective aggregation changes what dftracer does at the point of exit for calls matching the `dur < 1000` rule: instead of emitting a full event per call, it accumulates count/sum/min/max into a periodically-flushed aggregate record (every `DFTRACER_TRACE_INTERVAL_MS`). This removes the per-call event-construction/write cost for the overwhelming majority of calls (which are short, matching the rule) while still emitting full events for any call that exceeds 1ms (the genuinely interesting slow calls), which is why both the size reduction (>1GB -> <1MB/rank) and the qualitative return to near-linear `-n` scaling were observed together.

**Framework-level MCP tool fix credited (already applied, not part of this session's own deliverable):**
- `session_build_annotated`'s `build_subdir` parameter was silently ignored for cmake/autotools/meson builds (only the `custom_build_cmd` escape hatch honored it). Fixed in `src/dftracer_agents/mcp_tools/tools/session/session_tools.py`. **Pitfalls discovered and their exact fix (see full detail in `software-ygm`):**
- Header-only library + per-header `DFTRACER_CPP_*` usage requires `#include <dftracer/dftracer.h>` in EACH header, not just the entry `.cpp` (CP9).
- `FetchContent_MakeAvailable` silently falls through to a fresh unannotated clone unless `FETCHCONTENT_SOURCE_DIR_<NAME>` is set to the local annotated tree.
- Every dftracer-instrumented library needs its OWN `DFTRACER_CPP_INIT`/`FINI` per consuming binary — a header-only library's internal annotation alone is not self-sufficient.
- `YGM_COMM_IRECV_SIZE_KB` (singular) is the real env var; the plural form silently no-ops.

## 10. Recommendations for Future Runs

**What worked well:** the iterative bisection approach (rank-density sweep, then buffer-size fix, then aggregation fix) correctly isolated three independent problems that were initially conflated as "scaling doesn't work." Selective aggregation is a strong general pattern for any annotated async/actor-model progress-poll path — worth defaulting to whenever annotating a spin-poll hot loop, rather than defaulting to stripping annotation.

**What needs improvement:** this session skipped the standard `dfdiagnoser`/`comparator` MCP-tool chain in favor of manual wall-clock/hop-rate comparisons for its two headline findings — a future re-run of this same workload should run `session_diagnose_bottlenecks` and `comparator` against the `traces_agg_final/` data to get a formal severity score and a significance-flagged delta, rather than relying on qualitative "5-10x slower" language.

**Known limitations:**
- `flux proxy` was unreliable this session (hangs), forcing a raw `FLUX_URI=ssh://...` workaround for the final scaled run and leaving no saved launch script — now backfilled as `scripts/run_scaled_ygm_bench.sh`.
- `mcp__dftracer__view` quoted-string DSL queries are broken through this session's flux-proxy wrapper; `mcp__dftracer__reader(mode="lines")` rejects the documented default `start=0`.
